findings.title: Cyclic module dependency (9 modules)
findings.description: Modules form a compile/load-time cycle: src/engines/sandbox-runner -> src/router/router -> src/engines/provider-mux -> src/engines/composer-typing -> src/executor/fleet-supervisor -> src/engines/chrome-governor -> src/engines/capability-resolution -> src/engines/mirror-engine -> src/storage/contracts.
findings.evidence: cycle: engines/sandbox-runner -> router/router -> engines/provider-mux -> engines/composer-typing -> executor/fleet-supervisor -> engines/chrome-governor -> engines/capability-resolution -> engines/mirror-engine -> storage/contracts -> engines/sandbox-runner
findings.impact: Cycles complicate reasoning, break lazy init, and make refactoring risky.

fix.summary: Introduce an interface/contract module that the cycle participants depend on, or invert one of the dependency directions.
steps: Pick the edge whose direction is most easily inverted.
Extract the shared abstraction into a new foundation module.
Depend on the abstraction instead of the concrete module.
Re-run `audit-arch` to confirm the cycle is gone.
